Your rash is a pseudoallergic reaction.
This is a typical manifestation of helminthiasis.
And is it possible to say it humanly?
You simply have worms.
Are you serious? I have worms?
Well, it is not me who has them.
But where do I have worms from?

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence
Secondary conversational sense ('oh come on!') (ну, папа!) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
polite to one person, or to several people
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'здравлять'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to congratulate', forming an aspectual pair with 'поздравить'.
Russian determiner/pronoun ('your') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'rash' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Your rash is a pseudoallergic reaction.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('pseudo-allergic').

examples.trans: Your rash is a pseudoallergic reaction.

examples.text: Врач объяснил, что эта сыпь — псевдоаллергическая реакция.
examples.trans: The doctor explained that this rash is a pseudo-allergic reaction.

examples.text: Такой псевдоаллергический приступ быстро проходит после отдыха.
examples.trans: Such a pseudo-allergic episode passes quickly after rest.

meanings.note: International noun in '-ция' (from Latin '-tio'), feminine declension. Common feminine noun meaning 'reaction' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The reaction is positive. People like it.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('typical').

examples.trans: This is a typical manifestation of helminthiasis.

examples.text: Это совершенно типичное проявление весенней усталости.
examples.trans: This is a completely typical manifestation of spring fatigue.

examples.text: Перед нами типичный пример классической французской кулинарии.
examples.trans: Before us is a typical example of classic French cooking.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'явление'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'manifestation, display' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is a typical manifestation of helminthiasis.

examples.text: Это типичное проявление сильной пищевой аллергии.
examples.trans: This is a typical manifestation of a strong food allergy.

examples.text: Шеф ценит любое проявление честности и таланта в работе.
examples.trans: The chef values any display of honesty and talent at work.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'helminthiasis, worms' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is a typical manifestation of helminthiasis.
This is a typical manifestation of dangerous helminthiasis.

examples.text: Инспектор строго проверяет кухню на гельминтоз.
examples.trans: The inspector strictly checks the kitchen for helminthiasis.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('so, and what about') (starting a question: а жвачку?) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.en: in a human way, decently, fairly
meanings.note: не по-человечески = not right / not decently

examples.text: У нас с тобой не по-человечески всё пошло.
examples.trans: Things didn't go right between us.
Talk to me like a human being.

examples.text: Аркаша, у нас с тобой не по-человечески всё пошло.
examples.trans: Arkasha, things didn't go right between us.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'may'.
Secondary conversational sense ('it is possible') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?
Secondary conversational sense ('tell me / tell us') (polite request) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'at' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('I have') (possession) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('from (ask from someone)') (просить у кого) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'just'.
Secondary conversational sense ('easy') (это просто = it's easy) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Agent noun formed with the international suffix '-ист' denoting a specialist or adherent. Common masculine noun meaning 'parasitic worms' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Are you serious? I have worms?
But where do I have worms from?

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'seriously'.
goes right before the word it negates
emphatic at the start of a sentence
Secondary conversational sense ('? = really?, oh yeah?') (disbelief) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'куда').

examples.trans: Where does that word come from?
Thief, thief. Where does that word come from?

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'чина'). Common feminine noun meaning 'reason, cause' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Нет причин держать вас под арестом.
examples.trans: There is no reason to keep you under arrest.

examples.text: Нет причин держать вас под арестом. Сегодня вы выйдете отсюда.
examples.trans: There is no reason to keep you under arrest. Today you will walk out of here.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'can', forming an aspectual pair with 'смочь'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Secondary conversational sense ('there is, there are') (present есть; у меня есть = I have) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: forms the superlative: самый главный = the most important
Secondary conversational sense ('the very') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The most important thing is the people.
Do you know the main thing?

meanings.note: Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'нообразный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('diverse, varied').

examples.text: Ну, причины могут быть самые разнообразные.
examples.trans: Well, the causes can be the most diverse.

examples.text: Причины такого решения могут быть самые разнообразные.
examples.trans: The reasons for such a decision can be most varied.

examples.text: В новом сезоне у нас будет очень разнообразное десертное меню.
examples.trans: In the new season we will have a very diverse dessert menu.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('bad').

examples.text: Я вчера ел маринованные грибы. Может, один гриб был плохой.
examples.trans: Yesterday I ate pickled mushrooms. Maybe one mushroom was bad.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'hygiene' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Плохая гигиена или контакты с почвой.
examples.trans: Poor hygiene or contacts with soil.

examples.text: На кухне ресторана личная гигиена важнее всего.
examples.trans: In a restaurant kitchen, personal hygiene is most important of all.

examples.text: Шеф всегда требует идеальной гигиены от всех поваров.
examples.trans: The chef always demands perfect hygiene from all the cooks.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'or', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.
Common masculine noun meaning 'contact' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: All contacts go only through me.
Do you have his contact details?

examples.text: Будут разные провокации. Все контакты только через меня.
examples.trans: There will be various provocations. All contacts go only through me.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'ground, soil' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Плохая гигиена или контакты с почвой.
examples.trans: Poor hygiene or contacts with soil.

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'зможно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Возможно, наш главный гость приедет сегодня немного раньше.
examples.trans: Perhaps our main guest will arrive a little earlier today.

examples.text: Сделайте всё возможное, чтобы ужин прошёл на высшем уровне.
examples.trans: Do everything possible so that the dinner goes at the highest level.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to love, to like', paired with 'полюбить'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to like') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ырой'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('raw, damp').

examples.text: Возможно, вы любите есть сырую рыбу.
examples.trans: Perhaps, you like to eat raw fish.

examples.text: Давай, иди! А завтра он что принесёт? Сырное фондю?
examples.trans: Go on, get out! And tomorrow what will he bring? Cheese fondue?

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'fish', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: A big platter of fish and crabs.

examples.text: На ужин мы приготовили свежую рыбу.
examples.trans: For dinner we cooked fresh fish.

examples.text: У нас есть большая тарелка рыбы и крабов.
examples.trans: We have a big platter of fish and crabs.

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'sushi', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Тут есть пицца, суши и борщ.
examples.trans: They have pizza, sushi, and borscht here.
